question.problem:
Let $R=[1,7]\times [1,6]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=xy.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{1,3,5,7\},\,{P}_{2}=\{1,6\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14225859/assets/68270610704b1ef132469193e7948f54e548fa22223b6fc49b693753f998f874.png)

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{M}_{31}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{31}),
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=10$ for all $3$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =10\cdot {M}_{11}+10\cdot {M}_{21}+10\cdot {M}_{31} \\  & =10({M}_{11}+{M}_{21}+{M}_{31}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=xy$ increases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=xy$ increases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14225859/assets/7611c64cc460db725893156f6043644b34962a04f2aacef0b19cf99c5769cda3.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14225859/assets/75f378700ce6593a7ed9577b34e093cbbfe702e9512e9962e0d6f7f681694842.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{11} & =f(3,6)=18 \\ {M}_{21} & =f(5,6)=30 \\ {M}_{31} & =f(7,6)=42\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =10(18+30+42) \\  & =900.\end{aligned}
$$
